facts.claim: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built for the pharaoh Khufu
facts.context: Built around 2560 BC, give or take a few decades. It stayed the tallest structure made by humans for nearly 4,000 years.
facts.goDeeper: The workers left graffiti inside naming their own gangs, with names like 'Friends of Khufu'. They were proud of the job.

facts.claim: Howard Carter found the tomb of Tutankhamun
facts.context: Carter reached the sealed doorway in November 1922 after six years of searching the Valley of the Kings.
facts.goDeeper: Asked whether he could see anything through the first small hole, Carter answered: 'Yes, wonderful things.'

facts.claim: The Rosetta Stone was found by French soldiers in Egypt
facts.context: Soldiers in Napoleon's expedition uncovered it while rebuilding a fort near the town of Rashid.
facts.goDeeper: The British took it two years later as a spoil of war. It has been in the British Museum since 1802.

facts.claim: Champollion cracked the hieroglyphic script
facts.context: Jean-Francois Champollion announced his breakthrough in 1822, 23 years after the Rosetta Stone was found.
facts.goDeeper: Nobody had been able to read hieroglyphs for roughly 1,400 years. An entire civilisation's writing had gone silent.

facts.claim: Cleopatra died, ending three thousand years of pharaohs
facts.context: She died in 30 BC after Octavian's forces took Alexandria. Egypt became a Roman province.
facts.goDeeper: She was the last ruler of the Ptolemaic dynasty, and reportedly the first of them in three centuries who bothered to learn Egyptian.

facts.claim: Original height of the Great Pyramid
facts.context: About 146 metres when finished, roughly 480 feet. Erosion and the loss of its outer casing have taken some metres off.
facts.goDeeper: The base is level to within a couple of centimetres across more than five acres, achieved without a single modern instrument.

facts.claim: Length of the reign of Ramesses II
facts.context: He ruled for about 66 years in the 13th century BC and lived into his ninetieth year.
facts.goDeeper: He outlived twelve of his own sons. By the end of his reign, most Egyptians alive had never known another pharaoh.

facts.claim: The Battle of Kadesh was fought between Egypt and the Hittites
facts.context: Fought around 1274 BC, it may have been the largest chariot battle ever, with several thousand chariots.
facts.goDeeper: It ended in the earliest surviving peace treaty between two great powers. A copy hangs at the United Nations.

facts.claim: Upper and Lower Egypt were unified into one kingdom
facts.context: Traditionally dated to about 3100 BC and credited to a king named Narmer.
facts.goDeeper: The double crown of Egypt was two crowns combined, one for each half of the country, worn together for the next three millennia.

facts.claim: Hatshepsut began her reign as pharaoh
facts.context: She took power around 1479 BC and ruled for roughly two decades, one of very few women to rule Egypt outright.
facts.goDeeper: Her successor tried to erase her from the record, chiselling her name off monuments. It did not work.

facts.claim: Alexander the Great took Egypt from the Persians
facts.context: Egypt surrendered to him in 332 BC, and he founded Alexandria on the coast the following year.
facts.goDeeper: His general Ptolemy took Egypt after Alexander died, starting the dynasty that ended with Cleopatra 300 years later.

facts.claim: Number of scripts carved on the Rosetta Stone
facts.context: The same decree appears three times: in hieroglyphs, in demotic Egyptian, and in ancient Greek.
facts.goDeeper: Scholars could already read the Greek. That is what made the stone a key rather than just another inscription.

facts.claim: Tutankhamun's age when he died
facts.context: He became pharaoh at about nine and died at around nineteen.
facts.goDeeper: He was a minor king who was largely forgotten, which is exactly why his tomb survived intact while the great pharaohs' were robbed.

facts.claim: Length of the Nile
facts.context: About 6,650 km, or roughly 4,130 miles, running north through eleven countries.
facts.goDeeper: Egypt is mostly desert. Nearly everyone in the country has always lived within a few miles of that one river.

facts.claim: Number of known pyramids in Egypt
facts.context: Around 118 have been identified, though the count shifts as ruined ones are confirmed or reclassified.
facts.goDeeper: Sudan, just south of Egypt, has considerably more pyramids than Egypt does. They are smaller and much less famous.

facts.claim: Weight of Tutankhamun's gold funeral mask
facts.context: About 10 kg of solid gold, roughly 22 pounds, inlaid with lapis lazuli and coloured glass.
facts.goDeeper: The mask was only the outermost layer. His innermost coffin was another 110 kg of solid gold.

facts.claim: The pyramids were built by slave labour
facts.context: The evidence points to paid and conscripted Egyptian workers, housed and fed in purpose-built villages beside the site, not slaves.
facts.goDeeper: Archaeologists found the workers' bakeries and breweries, and their graves. Some had healed broken bones, meaning someone treated them.

facts.claim: Cleopatra was descended from Greeks, not Egyptians
facts.context: She belonged to the Ptolemaic line founded by one of Alexander's Macedonian generals, and the family ruled Egypt as Greeks for three centuries.
facts.goDeeper: She was reportedly the first Ptolemaic ruler to actually learn the Egyptian language, roughly 300 years in.

facts.claim: Hieroglyphs were pure picture-writing with no sounds attached
facts.context: Most hieroglyphs stand for sounds, not things. That was Champollion's insight and the reason the script could finally be read.
facts.goDeeper: The assumption that they were purely symbolic is what stalled European scholars for centuries.

facts.claim: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid
facts.context: The pyramid was already about 2,500 years old when she was born. The Moon landing came about 2,000 years after she died.
facts.goDeeper: Ancient Egypt was ancient to the ancient Egyptians. Cleopatra was a tourist at the pyramids in the same way we are.
